source.text: γίνεσθε οὖν μιμηταὶ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς τέκνα ἀγαπητά, καὶ περιπατεῖτε ἐν ἀγάπῃ, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν ἡμᾶς καὶ παρέδωκεν ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν προσφορὰν καὶ θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ εἰς ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας.

records.literal_gloss: Become therefore imitators of the God, as children beloved, \v 2 and walk in love, just as also the Christ loved us and gave up himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to the God for an aroma of fragrance.

en.L: Be imitators of God, therefore, as beloved children, \v 2 and walk in love, just as the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also loved us and gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a fragrant aroma.
en.B: So imitate God, since you are children {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dearly loves. \v 2 Let love guide the way you live, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} loved us and handed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} over for our sake, an offering and sacrifice to God, a fragrance that pleased {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: God loves you as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own dear children, so be like {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 2 Let love shape the way you live. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} loved us that way. He gave up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life for us. It was an offering to God, a sacrifice that pleased God like a sweet smell.

decisions.choice: imitators of God, as dearly loved children: children copy the Father who loves them
decisions.reason: οὖν ties this to 4:32: God in Christ forgave them, so they are to forgive and love as he does. Children take after their father; being his dearly loved children is the reason for imitating him, not the reward for it.

decisions.choice: walk: the way one lives
decisions.reason: περιπατεῖτε is Paul's usual picture for a whole way of life (2:10, 4:1, 4:17, 5:8, 5:15). Here the way of life is to be marked by love.

decisions.choice: an offering and a sacrifice, a fragrant aroma: Christ's death described in the language of the Old Testament sacrifices
decisions.reason: ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας is the phrase the Greek Old Testament uses for a sacrifice God accepts with pleasure (Genesis 8:21; Exodus 29:18; Leviticus 1:9). "Sacrifice and offering" are paired in Psalm 40:6. Paul uses the same phrase for the Philippians' gift (Philippians 4:18). Christ's self-giving is the offering God accepted.

decisions.choice: gave himself up for us: handed himself over on our behalf
decisions.reason: παρέδωκεν is used of Jesus being handed over to death (Romans 4:25; Galatians 2:20). He did it himself, and ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν says it was for our sake. Verse 25 says the same of his love for the church.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: Let love guide the way you live (B); Let love shape the way you live (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives (m2); Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: a fragrance that pleased him (B); a sacrifice that pleased God like a sweet smell (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the sacrifice language means (m3): God was pleased to accept it.

decisions.choice: gave up his life
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that giving himself up meant his death (m4).

source.text: Πορνεία δὲ καὶ ἀκαθαρσία πᾶσα ἢ πλεονεξία μηδὲ ὀνομαζέσθω ἐν ὑμῖν, καθὼς πρέπει ἁγίοις, καὶ αἰσχρότης καὶ μωρολογία ἢ εὐτραπελία, ἃ οὐκ ἀνῆκεν, ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον εὐχαριστία.

records.literal_gloss: Sexual immorality but and impurity all or greed not even let it be named among you, as is fitting for holy [ones], \v 4 and filthiness and foolish talk or coarse joking, which are not fitting, but rather thanksgiving.

en.L: But sexual immorality and all impurity or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for holy [ones], \v 4 and [neither] filthiness and foolish talk or coarse joking, which are not proper, but rather thanksgiving.
en.B: Sexual immorality, impurity of every kind, and greed must not even be spoken of as present among you; that is what suits God's holy people. \v 4 The same goes for shameful conduct, foolish talk and crude jokes. They do not belong. Let there be thanksgiving instead.
en.R: Do not let anyone be able to say that sexual sin, any kind of impure act, or greed is found among you. These things are wrong for God's people. \v 4 Do not take part in shameful things, foolish talk or dirty jokes. They are not right for you. Thank God instead.

decisions.choice: not even be named among you: so absent that no one could speak of them as present
alternatives: never to be spoken of at all
decisions.reason: μηδὲ ὀνομαζέσθω is a strong way of saying these things must have no place at all in the church. It is not a ban on ever mentioning them; Paul names them himself.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality, impurity, greed: the same three as in Colossians 3:5
decisions.reason: πορνεία is the general word for sexual sin, ἀκαθαρσία impurity of any kind, πλεονεξία the craving to have more. Next to sexual sins, greed may include wanting what belongs to another; verse 5 calls the greedy person an idolater, as Colossians 3:5 does.

decisions.choice: filthiness, foolish talk, coarse joking: shameful conduct and degrading speech
decisions.reason: αἰσχρότης is shamefulness, in deeds or in obscene words. μωρολογία is senseless talk. εὐτραπελία can mean ready wit, and Aristotle counts it a virtue (Nicomachean Ethics 4.8), but in a list beside filthiness it is wit that has turned coarse: jokes at the expense of what is decent.

decisions.choice: but rather thanksgiving: grateful speech takes the place of shameful speech
decisions.reason: No verb is given; the sense is "let there be thanksgiving". The mouth that might joke crudely is to thank God instead (5:20). εὐχαριστία also sounds like εὐτραπελία, which may be deliberate.

decisions.choice: holy ones: believers, God's holy people
decisions.reason: ἁγίοις is Paul's usual word for all believers as people set apart for God (1:1). What is fitting is measured by whose they are.

decisions.choice: God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The shared word list for Ephesians: Literal "holy [ones]".

decisions.choice: spoken of as present among you (B); Do not let anyone be able to say ... is found among you (R)
alternatives: not even be named among you
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the idiom (m1).

decisions.choice: Thank God
decisions.reason: Readable names God, to whom thanks is given (5:20).

source.text: τοῦτο γὰρ ἴστε γινώσκοντες ὅτι πᾶς πόρνος ἢ ἀκάθαρτος ἢ πλεονέκτης, ὅ ἐστιν εἰδωλολάτρης, οὐκ ἔχει κληρονομίαν ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This for know, knowing that every sexually immoral [person] or impure or greedy, which is an idolater, not has inheritance in the kingdom of the Christ and of God.

en.L: For know this, recognizing [it]: every sexually immoral or impure or greedy [person], that is, an idolater, has no inheritance in the kingdom of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and of God.
en.B: Be sure of this, and take it to heart: no one who is sexually immoral or impure, and no one who is greedy (for the greedy person is an idolater), has any inheritance in the kingdom of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and of God.
en.R: You can be sure of this: people who live in sexual sin, who do impure things, or who are greedy have no share in what God has promised to give in the kingdom that belongs to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and to God. A greedy person is really worshiping an idol.

decisions.choice: know this for sure: a command, made stronger by the doubled verb
alternatives: you know this, being aware that
decisions.reason: ἴστε can be a command ("know") or a statement ("you know"). The two verbs of knowing together press the point home. Either way Paul is telling them something he treats as certain.

decisions.choice: that is, an idolater: said of the greedy person
alternatives: said of all three kinds of people
decisions.reason: ὅ ἐστιν most naturally explains the last word, the greedy person. Colossians 3:5 says the same: greed is idolatry, because what a person craves above everything becomes their god (Matthew 6:24).

decisions.choice: the kingdom of Christ and of God: one kingdom, belonging to both
alternatives: the kingdom of the one who is Christ and God
decisions.reason: One article, τῇ, covers the whole phrase, so it is one kingdom that is Christ's and God's together (compare 1 Corinthians 15:24). Some have read the single article to mean "of the one who is Christ and God"; but θεοῦ often stands without an article, and Paul usually names Christ and God side by side.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share in what God gives his people
decisions.reason: κληρονομία is the share God gives his people (1:14, 1:18). The nouns πόρνος, ἀκάθαρτος and πλεονέκτης describe people by what marks their lives: such a way of life has no part in God's kingdom (1 Corinthians 6:9-10; Galatians 5:21).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: what God has promised to give
decisions.reason: The shared word list for Ephesians: Readable may explain "inheritance" (m4).

decisions.choice: an idolater (B); really worshiping an idol (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what an idolater is.

decisions.choice: the kingdom that belongs to Christ and to God
alternatives: the kingdom of Christ and of God
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear it is one kingdom (m3).

source.text: Μηδεὶς ὑμᾶς ἀπατάτω κενοῖς λόγοις, διὰ ταῦτα γὰρ ἔρχεται ἡ ὀργὴ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς τῆς ἀπειθείας.

records.literal_gloss: No one you let deceive with empty words, because of these things for comes the wrath of the God upon the sons of the disobedience.

en.L: Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the {{gender:children|sons}} of disobedience.
en.B: Do not let anyone mislead you with words that have nothing in them. These are the very things that bring the wrath of God on those who disobey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Do not let anyone trick you with empty talk. God's anger is coming because of these things, against people who refuse to obey {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: empty words: talk with no truth in it, here talk that makes light of these sins
decisions.reason: κενοῖς λόγοις are words with nothing behind them. After verse 5 the danger is talk that says these sins do not matter, or that God will not judge them.

decisions.choice: the wrath of God: God's settled judgment against evil
decisions.reason: ὀργὴ is God's just opposition to evil, not a loss of temper. It "comes": the final judgment is sure, and is already at work (Romans 1:18; Colossians 3:6).

decisions.choice: the sons of disobedience: people whose lives are marked by disobedience
decisions.reason: "Sons of" something is a Hebrew way of saying people characterized by it (2:2; compare "children of light", 5:8). It includes men and women.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children|sons}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means people of either sex (m3); "sons" is the traditional form. Balanced and Readable say "those who disobey", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: those who disobey him (B); people who refuse to obey him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom (m3) and name God as the one disobeyed.

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore become partners of them;

en.L: Therefore do not become partners with them.
en.B: So do not become their partners in what they do.
en.R: So do not join in with what those people do.

decisions.choice: partners with them: sharing in the disobedient people's way of life
alternatives: partners in these things (the sins of 5:3-5)
decisions.reason: αὐτῶν points back to "the sons of disobedience" (5:6). συμμέτοχοι is a sharer; in 3:6 the same word says the Gentiles share in the promise. Those who share in God's promise are not to share in the life that brings his wrath.

decisions.choice: in what they do
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the partnership would be in (m1).

source.text: ἦτε γάρ ποτε σκότος, νῦν δὲ φῶς ἐν κυρίῳ· ὡς τέκνα φωτὸς περιπατεῖτε, ὁ γὰρ καρπὸς τοῦ φωτὸς ἐν πάσῃ ἀγαθωσύνῃ καὶ δικαιοσύνῃ καὶ ἀληθείᾳ, δοκιμάζοντες τί ἐστιν εὐάρεστον τῷ κυρίῳ·

records.literal_gloss: You were for once darkness, now but light in [the] Lord; as children of light walk, \v 9 for the fruit of the light [is] in all goodness and righteousness and truth, \v 10 testing what is pleasing to the Lord;

en.L: For you were once darkness, but now [you are] light in [the] Lord. Walk as children of light \v 9 (for the fruit of the light [is] in all goodness and righteousness and truth), \v 10 testing what is pleasing to the Lord.
en.B: Once you were darkness itself; now, in the Lord, you are light. So conduct your lives as children of light. \v 9 What light produces is goodness, righteousness and truth of every kind. \v 10 Put things to the test, and learn what is pleasing to the Lord.
en.R: Once your whole life was darkness. But now you belong to the Lord, and you are light. So live like children of the light. \v 9 Light produces everything that is good, right and true. \v 10 Try to learn what pleases the Lord.

decisions.choice: you were darkness, now light: not only in the dark, but darkness itself; now light
decisions.reason: Paul does not say they were in darkness but that they were darkness, and are now light. What changed them is being "in the Lord", joined to Christ. Being light is who they now are; walking as children of light is the life that goes with it.

decisions.choice: children of light: people whose lives are marked by light
decisions.reason: Like "sons of disobedience" (5:6), "children of" something names people by what characterizes them (1 Thessalonians 5:5; John 12:36).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the fruit of the light"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, among them one early papyrus and many later ones, read "the fruit of the Spirit", probably from Galatians 5:22. "Light" fits the run of verses 8-14.

decisions.choice: testing: goes with "walk" in verse 8; verse 9 is an aside
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζοντες is a participle that belongs with the command "walk". Verse 9 explains what light produces, and verse 10 says how they are to walk: testing and finding out what the Lord approves (Romans 12:2).

decisions.choice: testing: examining in order to approve what is right
alternatives: testing in order to find fault
decisions.reason: δοκιμάζω is used for testing metal to prove it genuine. Here it is learning by testing, then choosing what pleases the Lord.

decisions.choice: conduct your lives (B); live (R)
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: good, right and true
decisions.reason: Readable turns the three nouns into plain adjectives; "right" stands for righteousness and "true" for truth.

decisions.choice: you belong to the Lord
decisions.reason: Readable says what "in the Lord" means here (m1).

source.text: καὶ μὴ συγκοινωνεῖτε τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἀκάρποις τοῦ σκότους, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐλέγχετε, τὰ γὰρ κρυφῇ γινόμενα ὑπ’ αὐτῶν αἰσχρόν ἐστιν καὶ λέγειν·

records.literal_gloss: And not share in the works the unfruitful of the darkness, rather but even expose [them], \v 12 for the things in secret being done by them shameful it is even to speak;

en.L: And do not take part in the unfruitful works of the darkness, but rather even expose [them], \v 12 for the things done by them in secret are shameful even to speak of.
en.B: Do not share in the deeds of darkness, which produce nothing good. Show them up for what they are instead. \v 12 The things those people do in secret are shameful even to speak of.
en.R: Do not join in the things people do in the dark. Those things produce nothing good. Instead, show them up for what they really are. \v 12 What those people do in secret is too shameful even to talk about.

decisions.choice: unfruitful: producing nothing good
decisions.reason: ἀκάρποις sets these works against "the fruit of the light" (5:9): darkness yields nothing worth having (Galatians 5:19-22 makes the same contrast between works and fruit).

decisions.choice: expose: bring into the open and show to be wrong
decisions.reason: ἐλέγχω means to bring something to light so that it is seen for what it is, and so to show it wrong or to convict. Verse 13 takes up the word: what is exposed is made visible by the light. The life of believers does this, and so may their words.

decisions.choice: for: these deeds are too shameful to talk about, so they are to be exposed, not discussed
decisions.reason: γὰρ gives the reason. The secret deeds of "them", the disobedient (5:6), are so shameful that even speaking of them is degrading; believers are not to dwell on them in talk, but to let the light show them up.

decisions.choice: those people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "them" are (m3).

source.text: τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐλεγχόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς φανεροῦται, πᾶν γὰρ τὸ φανερούμενον φῶς ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: The but all things being exposed by the light are made visible, \v 14 everything for that is made visible light is.

en.L: But all things, being exposed by the light, are made visible, \v 14 for everything that is made visible is light.
en.B: But when anything is exposed by the light, it is seen for what it is, \v 14 for whatever is brought into view becomes light.
en.R: But when the light shines on something, it shows what that thing really is. \v 14 And whatever the light shines on becomes light too.

decisions.choice: everything made visible is light: what the light shines on is itself changed into light
alternatives: whatever is made visible is in the light
it is light that makes everything visible
decisions.reason: The clause is short and hard. Read with verse 8 ("you were darkness, now light") and with the call that follows ("wake up ... Christ will shine on you"), it says that light does more than show things up: what it reaches, it changes, as it changed the readers. It could also mean simply that whatever is made visible is in the light, or that light is what makes things visible.

decisions.choice: exposed by the light: the light both exposes and makes visible
decisions.reason: ὑπὸ τοῦ φωτὸς stands between "exposed" and "made visible" and can go with either. The meaning is the same: the light is what brings hidden deeds into the open (5:11).

decisions.choice: becomes light
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the meaning decision (m1) takes "is light" to mean. Literal keeps "is light".

decisions.choice: when the light shines on something, it shows what that thing really is
alternatives: being exposed by the light, they are made visible
decisions.reason: Readable puts "exposed" and "made visible" into one plain picture.

source.text: διὸ λέγει· Ἔγειρε, ὁ καθεύδων, καὶ ἀνάστα ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν, καὶ ἐπιφαύσει σοι ὁ Χριστός.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore it says: Wake up, the [one] sleeping, and rise from the dead, and will shine on you the Christ.

en.L: Therefore it says, "Wake up, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} will shine on you."
en.B: So it says: "Sleeper, wake up! Get up from among the dead, and {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} will give you light."
en.R: That is why it says, "Wake up, you who are sleeping! Get up from among the dead! {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} will shine {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light on you."

decisions.choice: a quotation whose source is unknown
decisions.reason: "It says" is the formula Paul used for Psalm 68 in 4:8, but these words are not found in the Old Testament or in any known writing. Isaiah 26:19 ("awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust") and Isaiah 60:1 ("arise, shine, for your light has come") share its images of waking, rising and light.

decisions.choice: sleep and death: pictures of life without God
decisions.reason: Ephesians has already called the readers once "dead" in their sins (2:1, 2:5). The call to wake and rise is a call to the new life that Christ gives; the light he gives answers to "now you are light" (5:8).

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "Christ will shine on you"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts and early writers read a word that differs by one letter and means "you will touch Christ". It has little support, and "shine" fits the theme of light.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: give you light (B); shine his light on you (R)
decisions.reason: ἐπιφαύσει is to shine on, like the dawn. Balanced and Readable keep the picture of light in everyday words.

source.text: Βλέπετε οὖν ἀκριβῶς πῶς περιπατεῖτε, μὴ ὡς ἄσοφοι ἀλλ’ ὡς σοφοί, ἐξαγοραζόμενοι τὸν καιρόν, ὅτι αἱ ἡμέραι πονηραί εἰσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Watch therefore carefully how you walk, not as unwise but as wise, \v 16 buying up the time, because the days evil are.

en.L: Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise [people] but as wise, \v 16 buying up the time, because the days are evil.
en.B: So take great care how you live, not as people without wisdom but as people who have it. \v 16 Make good use of every opportunity, because the days are evil.
en.R: So be very careful about how you live. Do not live like foolish people. Live like wise people. \v 16 Use every chance you get to do good, because we live in evil days.

decisions.choice: buying up the time: making the most of each opportunity
alternatives: rescuing the time from evil use
decisions.reason: ἐξαγοράζω means to buy up, to buy out. With καιρόν, the right or opportune time, it means seizing every opening, as in Colossians 4:5. "Redeeming the time" has also been taken as rescuing time from evil use; the sense is close.

decisions.choice: the days are evil: the present age is marked by evil
decisions.reason: This is the age in which evil is at work (2:2; Galatians 1:4); 6:13 speaks of "the evil day". It is a reason to use the time well, not to withdraw.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "watch carefully how you walk"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have the two words the other way round: "watch how carefully you walk". The sense is much the same.

decisions.choice: live
decisions.reason: "Walk" is a figure for how one lives; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: Make good use of every opportunity (B); Use every chance you get to do good (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1). Readable's "to do good" names what the opportunity is for, as in Colossians 4:5.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο μὴ γίνεσθε ἄφρονες, ἀλλὰ συνίετε τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ κυρίου·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord [is];

en.L: Because of this, do not be foolish, but understand what the will of the Lord [is].
en.B: For this reason, do not be senseless. Come to understand what the Lord wants.
en.R: So do not be foolish. Learn what the Lord wants you to do.

decisions.choice: foolish: without sense, not thinking
decisions.reason: ἄφρονες are people who do not use the judgment they have. The opposite is not cleverness but understanding the Lord's will, as "wise" is the opposite of "unwise" in verse 15.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "the will of the Lord"
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "the will of God", and one early papyrus "the will of Christ". In Ephesians "the Lord" is Christ (5:10, 5:19-20); the meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: what the Lord wants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "will" in everyday words.

source.text: καὶ μὴ μεθύσκεσθε οἴνῳ, ἐν ᾧ ἐστιν ἀσωτία, ἀλλὰ πληροῦσθε ἐν πνεύματι, λαλοῦντες ἑαυτοῖς ψαλμοῖς καὶ ὕμνοις καὶ ᾠδαῖς πνευματικαῖς, ᾄδοντες καὶ ψάλλοντες τῇ καρδίᾳ ὑμῶν τῷ κυρίῳ, εὐχαριστοῦντες πάντοτε ὑπὲρ πάντων ἐν ὀνόματι τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί, ὑποτασσόμενοι ἀλλήλοις ἐν φόβῳ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And not be drunk with wine, in which is wastefulness, but be filled in [the] Spirit, \v 19 speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and songs spiritual, singing and making music in the heart of you to the Lord, \v 20 giving thanks always for all things in [the] name of the Lord of us Jesus Christ to the God and Father, \v 21 submitting to one another in [the] fear of Christ.

en.L: And do not get drunk with wine, in which is reckless living, but be filled by [the] Spirit, \v 19 speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making music with your heart to the Lord, \v 20 giving thanks always for all things in [the] name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} to God the Father, \v 21 submitting to one another in [the] fear of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Do not get drunk on wine, for that is reckless, wasteful living. Instead, let the Spirit fill you. \v 19 Then you will speak to one another in psalms, hymns and Spirit-given songs, and sing and make music to the Lord with your hearts. \v 20 You will give thanks to God the Father at all times and for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 21 And you will submit to one another in the reverent fear of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Do not get drunk on wine. Being drunk leads to a wild and wasted life. Instead, let God's Spirit fill you. \v 19 Then you will speak to each other with psalms, hymns and other songs that the Spirit gives. You will sing and make music to the Lord from your hearts. \v 20 You will always thank God the Father for everything, as people who belong to our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. \v 21 And you will submit to one another, because you stand in awe of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: reckless living: a life thrown away
decisions.reason: ἀσωτία is wasteful, uncontrolled living; the related adverb describes how the younger son wasted his money in Luke 15:13. ἐν ᾧ points to getting drunk on wine: that is where such living lies (Proverbs 23:31-35).

decisions.choice: be filled by the Spirit: the Spirit is the one who fills; what fills them is left open
alternatives: filled with the Spirit (the Spirit is what fills them)
decisions.reason: ἐν πνεύματι could mean the means (filled by the Spirit) or the content (filled with the Spirit); it could even mean their own spirit. Elsewhere in Ephesians ἐν πνεύματι usually means "by the Spirit" (2:22, 3:5, 6:18), and the prayer of 3:19 is that they be filled "to all the fullness of God". The contrast with wine is that something other than drink should control them. The command is in the present tense: go on being filled.

decisions.choice: speaking, singing, making music, giving thanks, submitting: what being filled by the Spirit produces
alternatives: separate commands: speak, sing, give thanks, submit
decisions.reason: The five participles hang on "be filled" and describe what a Spirit-filled church looks like. The last of them, "submitting to one another", is also the verb that verse 22 borrows, so the instructions to the household (5:22-6:9) stand under this same command.

decisions.choice: psalms, hymns and spiritual songs, spoken to one another: every kind of song the church sings
decisions.reason: ἑαυτοῖς here means "to one another", as in Colossians 3:16. The three words overlap: psalms, hymns of praise and other songs, all given by the Spirit (πνευματικαῖς). Singing builds up the church as well as praising God.

decisions.choice: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: as his people, through him
decisions.reason: To do something in someone's name is to do it as one who belongs to them and stands under their authority (Colossians 3:17). Thanks reaches God the Father through Jesus.

decisions.choice: submitting to one another: every believer places themselves under others
alternatives: each to those placed over them, as 5:22-6:9 set out
decisions.reason: ὑποτασσόμενοι is middle, an act of one's own will, as in Colossians 3:18. ἀλλήλοις, "one another", is addressed to the whole church. Verses 5:22-6:9 then apply it within the household; how far it runs both ways between wives and husbands, children and parents, slaves and masters is read differently.

decisions.choice: the fear of Christ: reverent awe toward Christ as Lord
decisions.reason: φόβος is fear, here the awe owed to Christ, who is Lord and will judge (2 Corinthians 5:10-11). It is the reason for submitting to one another. The same word comes back for the wife in 5:33.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in the fear of Christ"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "in the fear of God". The earliest have "Christ".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: let the Spirit fill you (B); let God's Spirit fill you (R)
decisions.reason: Naming the Spirit as the one who fills follows the meaning decision (m2) and keeps the content open.

decisions.choice: Then you will ... You will ... And you will
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the participles into sentences, and the words "then you will" keep them tied to "let the Spirit fill you" (m3) rather than making them new commands.

decisions.choice: God the Father
decisions.reason: One article covers "God and Father": one person, God who is the Father.

decisions.choice: as people who belong to our Lord Jesus Christ
alternatives: in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m5).

decisions.choice: in the reverent fear of (B); because you stand in awe of (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear the fear is reverence for Christ (m7), not terror.

source.text: Αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι ἀνήρ ἐστιν κεφαλὴ τῆς γυναικὸς ὡς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς κεφαλὴ τῆς ἐκκλησίας, αὐτὸς σωτὴρ τοῦ σώματος.

records.literal_gloss: The wives to the own husbands as to the Lord, \v 23 because [a] husband is head of the wife as also the Christ [is] head of the church, he [is] savior of the body.

en.L: Wives, [submit] to your own husbands as to the Lord, \v 23 because [the] husband is head of the wife as the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also [is] head of the church, [and] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} [is the] Savior of the body.
en.B: Wives should submit to their own husbands, as to the Lord. \v 23 For the husband is head of the wife, just as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is head of the church; and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Savior of that body.
en.R: Wives, submit to your own husbands, as you would to the Lord. \v 23 For a husband is the head of his wife, just as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is the head of the church. The church is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who saves it.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no verb of its own in verse 22
alternatives: "Wives, let them submit to their own husbands"
decisions.reason: In the SBLGNT, as in the earliest witnesses (an early papyrus and Codex Vaticanus), verse 22 has no verb and takes "submitting" from verse 21. Most other manuscripts add one, some "submit" (ὑποτάσσεσθε) and others "let them submit" (ὑποτασσέσθωσαν), not always in the same place. The meaning is the same; the shorter text binds the verse more closely to 5:21.

decisions.choice: the verb is "submitting" from 5:21: wives' submission is the first case of the submission asked of all believers
decisions.reason: Verse 22 needs the participle of verse 21 to make sense, so the two belong together: what verse 21 asks of everyone, verse 22 applies to wives toward their own husbands. ὑποτάσσω in the middle is to place oneself under another by one's own choice (Colossians 3:18). It is a different verb from "obey", which Paul uses for children and slaves (6:1, 6:5).

decisions.choice: the household rules: Paul speaks to each member of the household
decisions.reason: Writers of the time set out the duties of household members (Aristotle, Politics 1.3), usually addressed to the man at its head. Paul speaks directly to wives, children and slaves, and gives husbands, fathers and masters duties too (5:25, 6:4, 6:9). He gives husbands the longest section (5:25-33). Colossians 3:18-4:1 is the shorter parallel.

decisions.choice: as to the Lord: as part of their service to the Lord
alternatives: as if the husband were the Lord
decisions.reason: ὡς τῷ κυρίῳ says how wives are to submit: as something done for the Lord. Slaves are told the same in 6:7, "as to the Lord and not to people". It does not put the husband in the Lord's place.

decisions.choice: head: the one who leads, as Christ leads and gives himself for the church
decisions.reason: κεφαλή is the head of a body. In Ephesians Christ is head over all things for the church (1:22), and the body grows from him (4:15-16). Here headship is tied to submission (5:24), so it includes leading; and the comparison with Christ defines it as leadership that saves, loves and gives itself (5:23, 5:25). Some read κεφαλή here mainly as "source".

decisions.choice: he is the Savior of the body: said of Christ alone
alternatives: the husband too is his wife's protector
decisions.reason: αὐτὸς σωτὴρ is emphatic: Christ himself is the one who saved the church, his body. The comparison with the husband does not extend to this, and verse 24 begins with "but". Some read it as a picture of the husband as protector of his wife.

decisions.choice: [submit] (L); should submit (B); submit (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is understood from verse 21 (m1, m2). Readable keeps "submit" here, unlike "follow your husbands' lead" in Colossians 3:18, because the word is shared with verse 21.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: The church is his body, and he is the one who saves it
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the body" is (5:30; 1:23).

source.text: ἀλλὰ ὡς ἡ ἐκκλησία ὑποτάσσεται τῷ Χριστῷ, οὕτως καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τοῖς ἀνδράσιν ἐν παντί.

records.literal_gloss: But as the church submits to the Christ, so also the wives to the husbands in everything.

en.L: But as the church submits to the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, so also the wives [should submit] to [their] husbands in everything.
en.B: But in the same way that the church submits to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, wives are also to submit to their husbands in everything.
en.R: But the church submits to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. In the same way, wives should submit to their husbands in everything.

decisions.choice: but: Christ alone is Savior, yet the comparison holds for submission
decisions.reason: ἀλλὰ follows "he is the Savior of the body" (5:23). The husband is not his wife's savior, but the church's submission to Christ is still the pattern for the wife's submission to her husband.

decisions.choice: submits: the church places itself under Christ
decisions.reason: ὑποτάσσεται can be middle ("submits") or passive ("is subjected"). As in 5:21, the middle fits: the church gives itself to Christ's rule.

decisions.choice: wives to their husbands: the verb is understood again
decisions.reason: As in verse 22, the Greek leaves out the verb for wives; "submit" is carried over from the first half of the sentence.

decisions.choice: in everything: in every area of shared life
decisions.reason: ἐν παντί means in all things, not in some only. The frame Paul has set is "as to the Lord" (5:22) and "as the church to Christ".

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: [should submit] (L); are to submit, should submit (B, R)
decisions.reason: The verb is understood (m3).

source.text: Οἱ ἄνδρες, ἀγαπᾶτε τὰς γυναῖκας, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς ἠγάπησεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν καὶ ἑαυτὸν παρέδωκεν ὑπὲρ αὐτῆς, ἵνα αὐτὴν ἁγιάσῃ καθαρίσας τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ ὕδατος ἐν ῥήματι, ἵνα παραστήσῃ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ ἔνδοξον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, μὴ ἔχουσαν σπίλον ἢ ῥυτίδα ἤ τι τῶν τοιούτων, ἀλλ’ ἵνα ᾖ ἁγία καὶ ἄμωμος.

records.literal_gloss: The husbands, love the wives, just as also the Christ loved the church and himself gave up for her, \v 26 so that her he might make holy, cleansing [her] by the washing of the water in [the] word, \v 27 so that might present he to himself glorious the church, not having spot or wrinkle or any of the such things, but that she might be holy and blameless.

en.L: Husbands, love [your] wives, just as the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also loved the church and gave {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} up for her, \v 26 so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might make her holy, cleansing [her] by the washing of the water with [the] word, \v 27 so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might present the church to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} glorious, not having spot or wrinkle or any such things, but that she might be holy and blameless.
en.B: Husbands, love your wives the way {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} loved the church and handed {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} over for her. \v 26 He did this to make her holy, cleansing her by the washing of water with the word, \v 27 so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might bring the church to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} in glory, with no spot or wrinkle or any flaw like that, but holy and without blame.
en.R: Husbands, love your wives just as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} loved the church. He gave up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} life for her \v 26 to make her holy. He made her clean by washing her with water and by God's word. \v 27 He did this so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could bring the church to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} glorious and beautiful, with no stain or wrinkle or any other flaw. He wanted her to be holy and without fault.

decisions.choice: love: self-giving love, measured by Christ's
decisions.reason: ἀγαπάω is the love God shows and asks of his people. It is not a usual word in household rules of the time (Colossians 3:19). Here its measure is Christ, who gave himself up for the church (5:2).

decisions.choice: so that ... so that ... that: three purposes of Christ's self-giving
decisions.reason: Christ gave himself to make the church holy (26), to present her to himself in glory (27), and so that she would be holy and blameless (27). The last echoes 1:4, where God chose his people to be "holy and blameless".

decisions.choice: the washing of water: probably baptism, pictured as a bride's bath before the wedding
alternatives: spiritual cleansing only, with no reference to baptism
decisions.reason: λουτρῷ is a bath or washing. The cleansing that belongs to Christ's people is pictured in baptism (1 Corinthians 6:11; Titus 3:5). The picture of a bride washed for her husband recalls Ezekiel 16:8-14, where God washes Jerusalem with water and makes her beautiful. Some read it only as a picture of spiritual cleansing, without a reference to baptism.

decisions.choice: with the word: the spoken word of God, the gospel
decisions.reason: ῥῆμα is a spoken word. In 6:17 "the word of God" uses the same noun. The cleansing comes with the message of Christ believed and confessed (Romans 10:8-9). It could also be the words spoken at baptism.

decisions.choice: present the church to himself: like a bridegroom receiving his bride
decisions.reason: παραστήσῃ is the word Paul uses for presenting a bride (2 Corinthians 11:2). Here Christ himself prepares the bride and receives her. "Spot or wrinkle" describes the bride's flawless beauty; ἔνδοξον, glorious, says she shares his glory.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: gave up his life
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that giving himself up meant his death.

decisions.choice: by God's word
decisions.reason: Readable says whose word it is, following m4.

decisions.choice: in glory (B); glorious and beautiful (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "beautiful" to carry the bridal picture (m5).

source.text: οὕτως ὀφείλουσιν καὶ οἱ ἄνδρες ἀγαπᾶν τὰς ἑαυτῶν γυναῖκας ὡς τὰ ἑαυτῶν σώματα· ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα ἑαυτὸν ἀγαπᾷ, οὐδεὶς γάρ ποτε τὴν ἑαυτοῦ σάρκα ἐμίσησεν, ἀλλὰ ἐκτρέφει καὶ θάλπει αὐτήν, καθὼς καὶ ὁ Χριστὸς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, ὅτι μέλη ἐσμὲν τοῦ σώματος αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: So ought also the husbands to love the of themselves wives as the of themselves bodies. The [one] loving the of himself wife himself loves, \v 29 no one for ever the of himself flesh hated, but nourishes and cherishes it, just as also the Christ the church, \v 30 because members we are of the body of him.

en.L: In this way husbands also ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. He who loves his own wife loves himself, \v 29 for no one ever hated his own flesh, but [he] nourishes and cherishes it, just as the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} also [does] the church, \v 30 because we are members of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.
en.B: So husbands are bound to love their wives as their own bodies. To love one's wife is to love oneself. \v 29 Nobody has ever hated his own flesh; instead, he feeds it and looks after it, as {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} does for the church, \v 30 because we are parts of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.
en.R: In the same way, husbands should love their wives, because a wife is like her husband's own body. A man who loves his wife is loving himself. \v 29 No one hates his own body. People feed their bodies and take care of them. {{christos:Christ|The Messiah}} does the same for the church. \v 30 We are all parts of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body.

decisions.choice: in this way: as Christ loved the church (5:25-27), and as one's own body
alternatives: only forward: love them as their own bodies
decisions.reason: οὕτως looks back to Christ's love just described, and also forward to "as their own bodies". καὶ, "also", ties the husbands' love to Christ's.

decisions.choice: as their own bodies: because the wife is one body with her husband
alternatives: in the same way as they love their own bodies
decisions.reason: ὡς here means "as being" more than "in the same way as": the wife is, as it were, the husband's own body, as the church is Christ's body. The next clause ("loves himself") and the quotation of Genesis 2:24 ("one flesh", 5:31) point this way.

decisions.choice: flesh: one's own body
decisions.reason: σάρκα here is simply the body, with nothing of the sinful sense the word has elsewhere (2:3). The word prepares for "one flesh" in verse 31.

decisions.choice: nourishes and cherishes: feeds it and cares for it tenderly
decisions.reason: ἐκτρέφει is to feed and bring up (6:4 uses it of children); θάλπει is to keep warm, used of a nursing mother caring for her children (1 Thessalonians 2:7). Christ cares for the church in this way.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "because we are members of his body"
alternatives: "because we are members of his body, of his flesh and of his bones"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "of his flesh and of his bones", from Genesis 2:23. The earliest witnesses do not have the words.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: parts
decisions.reason: "Members" of a body now sounds like members of a club; Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: body
decisions.reason: Readable says what "flesh" means here (m3). Literal and Balanced keep "flesh" for its link with verse 31.

decisions.choice: because a wife is like her husband's own body
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the meaning decision (m2).

source.text: ἀντὶ τούτου καταλείψει ἄνθρωπος τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ προσκολληθήσεται τῇ γυναικὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσονται οἱ δύο εἰς σάρκα μίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this will leave a man the father and the mother and will be joined to the wife of him, and will be the two into flesh one.

en.L: For this reason a man will leave [his] father and mother and will be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.
en.B: This is why a man will leave his father and mother and cling to his wife, and the two will be one flesh.
en.R: As the Scriptures say, "That is why a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife. And the two of them will become one, like one body."

decisions.choice: a quotation of Genesis 2:24
decisions.reason: Paul quotes Genesis 2:24 in the form of the Greek Old Testament, which has "the two" where the Hebrew has "they". He differs from it slightly: a different word for "for this reason", and "his" is not repeated with father and mother. Jesus quotes the same verse on marriage (Matthew 19:5; Mark 10:7-8), and Paul in 1 Corinthians 6:16.

decisions.choice: for this reason: in Genesis, because the woman was taken from the man; here, read alongside Christ and the church
decisions.reason: In Genesis the words follow the making of the woman from the man's body. Paul quotes them right after "we are members of his body" (5:30), and verse 32 says he is speaking of Christ and the church.

decisions.choice: become one flesh: one shared life, including the bodily union of marriage
decisions.reason: εἰς σάρκα μίαν follows a Hebrew way of saying "become". "Flesh" means a body, a person or a family: husband and wife become one new life, closer than their ties to their parents (as in Genesis 2:24).

decisions.choice: be joined: hold fast, in lasting loyalty
decisions.reason: προσκολληθήσεται is to be glued or bound fast to someone. The Hebrew verb in Genesis 2:24 is also used for Israel's loyalty to God (Deuteronomy 10:20).

decisions.choice: As the Scriptures say
decisions.reason: Readable marks the quotation (m1), which the Greek gives without an introduction.

decisions.choice: become one, like one body
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m3), as Genesis 2:24 does in this translation.

decisions.choice: cling to
decisions.reason: Says the strength of the verb (m4) in everyday words.

source.text: τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο μέγα ἐστίν, ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν.

records.literal_gloss: The mystery this great is, I but speak with reference to Christ and to the church.

en.L: This mystery is great, but I am speaking with reference to {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and to the church.
en.B: There is a great mystery here, but I am speaking about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and the church.
en.R: This is a great mystery, a truth once hidden that God has now made known. I am saying it is about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and the church.

decisions.choice: mystery: a truth once hidden in God's purpose, now made known
decisions.reason: In Ephesians μυστήριον is God's plan, hidden before and now revealed (1:9, 3:3-6). Here it is the deeper meaning of Genesis 2:24: the union of husband and wife points to the union of Christ and the church. The Latin Vulgate translated the word sacramentum, but the Greek word does not name a rite.

decisions.choice: great: of great importance and depth
decisions.reason: μέγα says the mystery is weighty, not that it is very hard to understand.

decisions.choice: I am speaking with reference to Christ and the church: this is what the mystery chiefly concerns
decisions.reason: ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς sets Paul's own application beside the plain sense of Genesis 2:24. He does not deny that it speaks of marriage; verse 33 turns straight back to husbands and wives. But the great mystery is Christ and the church.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article where the Greek has it: "the [[CL]]".

decisions.choice: a truth once hidden that God has now made known
decisions.reason: The shared word list for Ephesians: Readable may explain "mystery" (m1).

source.text: πλὴν καὶ ὑμεῖς οἱ καθ’ ἕνα ἕκαστος τὴν ἑαυτοῦ γυναῖκα οὕτως ἀγαπάτω ὡς ἑαυτόν, ἡ δὲ γυνὴ ἵνα φοβῆται τὸν ἄνδρα.

records.literal_gloss: Nevertheless also you, the [ones] one by one, each the of himself wife so let him love as himself, the and wife that she respect the husband.

en.L: Nevertheless, you also, one by one, let each love his own wife as himself, and the wife [is to see] that she respects [her] husband.
en.B: But to return to you: each husband must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must see to it that she respects her husband.
en.R: But what I have said is for each one of you as well. Every husband must love his wife as he loves himself. And every wife must respect her husband.

decisions.choice: nevertheless: leaving the mystery, back to husbands and wives
decisions.reason: πλὴν turns from Christ and the church (5:32) to what it means for each married couple. However great the mystery, the duty is plain.

decisions.choice: that she respect: a command
decisions.reason: ἵνα with the verb here works as a command, as it sometimes does (compare 2 Corinthians 8:7). It matches "let him love" in the first half.

decisions.choice: respect: honor with reverence
decisions.reason: φοβῆται is the verb "to fear". Here it is not being afraid but the honor that belongs to the one she submits to, of the same family as "the fear of Christ" (5:21). Peter uses the same word in 1 Peter 3:2.

decisions.choice: love her as himself: an echo of Leviticus 19:18
decisions.reason: "Love your neighbor as yourself" (Leviticus 19:18) now applies to the nearest neighbor of all, who is one flesh with him (5:28-31).

decisions.choice: respect
decisions.reason: "Fear" would suggest being afraid (m3).

decisions.choice: each husband (B); Every husband (R)
decisions.reason: "Each" refers to the husbands just addressed.
